# Burn record — external release gate run `33293517671`

Recorded: 2026-08-30, immediately after the run and before any repair was applied.

## Outcome

**INVALID — apparatus failure. No candidate output was produced and nothing about the candidate
was measured.**

## What happened

The run reached the authoring step and stopped there. Zero Gemini calls were made; the scored
gate step was skipped by the runner's own `set -e`, and no artifact was produced.

```
AUTHOR_PROVIDER_FAILURE: Groq HTTP 403: {"title":"Error 1010: Access denied","status":403,
"detail":"The site owner has blocked access based on your browser's signature.",
"error_code":1010,"error_name":"browser_signature_banned","retryable":false,
"what_you_should_do":"**Do not retry.** Your user-agent has been banned by the site owner."}
```

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| Deterministic checks before any credential | success |
| Author isolation assertion | success (`EXTERNAL_AUTHOR_ISOLATION_PASS`) |
| Credential presence | success — all three secrets present |
| Author and seal the external pack | **failure**, 1 second in |
| Run the preregistered external release gate | skipped |

## Root cause

Mine, in the harness, not the provider and not the candidate.

`author_external_heldout_v1.py` built its Groq request with `urllib.request.Request` and did not
set a `User-Agent`, so the request went out as `Python-urllib/3.11`. Cloudflare rejects that
signature on `api.groq.com` with error 1010. Every working Groq call already in this repository
sets an explicit agent — `author_sealed_heldout_r2.py:194` sends
`'User-Agent': 'visual-heldout-r2-audit/0.1'`. I omitted it.

This is a transport-layer configuration defect. It is **not** evidence that Groq is ineligible as
the authoring family: the block is on the agent string, not on quota, payload size or account
state, and the response never reached the Groq API at all.

## Repair

One line: an explicit `User-Agent` header on the authoring request, with a comment naming this
run so the reason survives.

Nothing else changed. The candidate, the professional model, the grader, the classifier, the
output contract, the fixture contract, the authoring schemas, the admission checks, the oracle,
the tier map, both tier-2 caps, the tier-1 zero tolerance and the trial count are all untouched.
The `author` blob in `preregistration-external-2026-09-02.json` is re-bound to the repaired file,
which is the only field of the preregistration that moves.

## Why re-running is legitimate here

`preregistration-external-2026-09-02.json` `post_gate_policy` forbids automatic repair and rerun
**after a result**. There is no result to protect: no case was authored, no candidate call was
made, no trial was recorded, and no ledger exists. The preregistration's own `INVALID` definition
covers exactly this — "the measurement apparatus failed … no candidate output exists, so there is
nothing to score" — and states that the cycle may proceed once the apparatus fault is fixed.

Issue #189 says the same: *"If apparatus failure, mark INVALID rather than candidate FAIL."*

The precedent in this cycle is `68f7da4`, which repaired the two-tier workflow's runner invocation
between a failed dispatch and the scored run that produced the passed ledger.

## What no one may conclude from this run

Nothing about the candidate. It was never asked a question.
